Git branching is a powerful feature of version control that helps teams work together without conflicts. Instead of everyone editing the same code, each person creates a separate *feature branch* for their task, such as adding a new button or fixing a bug. This keeps the main project stable while they experiment.

Once the work is finished, the developer submits a *pull request*. This is a formal request for teammates to review the changes, discuss them, and test them before anything is finalized. After approval, the branch is *merged* into the main codebase. This simple workflow—branch, review, merge—makes collaboration efficient and reduces errors, ensuring the main version always remains reliable.
